title: Combined single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry analysis in intact murine dorsal root ganglia and sciatic nerve
protocol: Set the cryostat to −23°C.
Place tissue blocks frozen in OCT inside the cryostat.
Allow 1 h for the blocks to reach −23°C.
Mount the blocks onto the cryostat chuck.
Align tissue block with cryostat blade to ensure sectioning occurs parallel to the bottom of the block.
Cryosection the blocks by cutting 12 μm thick sections.
Use fine paint brushes to prevent or uncurl the tissue sections.
Thaw-mount tissue sections onto room temperature SuperFrost Plus slides for DRG tissue and poly-lysine adhesion coated slides for sciatic nerve tissue.
Air dry DRG tissue slides at room temperature for 60 - 120 minutes.
Air dry sciatic nerve tissue slides at room temperature overnight (12 - 16 hours).
Store dried slides at −80°C for up to three months if not immediately processed.
Acclimate the slides stored at −80°C in a 37°C incubator for 30-60 minutes.
Wash the slides with 1× RNase-free PBS in a slide rack at room temperature (20°C–24°C) for 5 minutes on a rotary shaker with gentle rotation.
Remove excess PBS by suction using a vacuum line fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Add 4-6 drops of RNAscope Hydrogen Peroxide to cover all the sections and allow to sit for 10 minutes exactly.
Gently tap the bottom edge of the slide against an absorbent towel to remove the RNAscope Hydrogen Peroxide solution.
Immediately wash the slides with DEPC-H2O in a slide rack at room temperature for 2 minutes on a rotary shaker.
Wash again with DEPC-H2O for 2 minutes at room temperature on a rotary shaker.
Fill the Steamer water reservoir with cold tap water.
Place a clear Steaming Bowl onto the base.
Place two slide racks into the bowl.
Fill one slide rack with 200 mL of RNAscope 1× Target Retrieval Reagent.
Fill the other slide rack with 200 mL of DEPC-H2O.
Turn on the Steamer.
Block all vent holes to prevent escape of steam.
Allow temperature to rise to at least 97°C.
Insert a thermometer into the container containing RNA scope 1× Target Retrieval Reagent to check temperature.
Add slides to the slide rack containing DEPC-H2O for 10 seconds.
Transfer slides into the slide rack containing RNAscope 1× Target Retrieval Reagent.
Block any vent holes to prevent escape of steam and treat for 5 min.
Remove slides from the steamer and transfer immediately to a separate rinse slide rack filled with DEPC-H2O.
Rinse slides for 15 seconds.
Transfer slides to a slide rack filled with RNase-free 100% ethanol for 3 minutes.
Dry slides at room temperature.
Draw a barrier of 20mm × 20mm around each section on the slide with the ImmEdge hydrophobic barrier pen.
Draw each outline 2–4 times to ensure a continuous barrier.
Do not touch the tissue section.
Dry slides completely for 5 min to 18 hours at room temperature.
Turn on the HybEZ Oven and set its temperature to 40°C.
Place the dried slides into the HybEZ slide tray.
Add approximately one drop per section of RNAscope Protease III to entirely cover each tissue section.
Load the slide tray into the oven.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 40°C.
Remove RNAscope Protease III solution by tapping the bottom edge of the slide against an absorbent towel.
Immediately wash the slides with DEPC-H2O in a slide rack at room temperature for 2 minutes on a rotary shaker (30 - 40 rpm).
Wash the slides with fresh DEPC-H2O for 2 min at room temperature on a rotary shaker.
Pre-warm RNAscope Probe Solution for 10 min in a 37°C incubator or water bath, ensuring any white precipitate is dissolved.
Cool the pre-warmed solution to room temperature (20°C - 24°C).
If dilution of probe is required, dilute it with RNAscope Probe Dilution Buffer at a ratio of 1:50.
For hybridizing multiple probes on one section, combine all probes in RNAscope Probe Dilution Buffer at a ratio of 1:50 to create a master mix.
Diluted probes may be stored at 2°C - 8°C for up to 6 months.
Remove any excess liquid by suctioning the liquid with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette to maintain gentle suction.
Place the slides into the HybEZ slide tray and add about one drop (∼50 μl) per 20 mm × 20 mm section of the diluted probes to entirely cover the tissue.
Load the slide tray into the oven and incubate for 2 h at 40°C.
Wash the slides with 1× RNAscope Wash Buffer in a slide rack for 2 min at RT on a rotary shaker (30 - 40 rpm).
Wash again with fresh 1× Wash Buffer for 2 min at RT on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Pre-warm the RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 AMP 1 solution for 10 min in a 37°C incubator, then cool to RT.
Hybridize AMP 1 by adding one drop per section of RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 AMP 1 solution to entirely cover the tissue.
Remove excess liquid from the slides by suctioning the liquid with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette to maintain gentle suction.
Load the slide tray into the oven and incubate for 30 min at 40°C.
Wash the slides with 1× Wash Buffer in a slide rack for 2 min at RT on a rotary shaker (30 - 40 rpm).
Wash again with fresh 1× Wash Buffer for 2 min at RT on a rotary shaker (30 - 40 rpm).
Pre-warm the RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 AMP 2 solution for 10 min in a 37°C incubator, then cool to 20°C–24°C.
Hybridize AMP 2.
Remove excess liquid from the slides by suctioning with a vacuum line fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Place the slides into the slide tray and add one drop per section of RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 AMP 2 solution to entirely cover the tissue.
Load the slide tray into the oven and incubate for 30 min at 40°C.
Wash the slides with 1× Wash Buffer in a slide rack for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30-40 rpm).
Wash again with fresh 1× Wash Buffer for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30-40 rpm).
Pre-warm the RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 AMP 3 solution for 10 min in a 37°C incubator, then cool to 20°C–24°C.
Hybridize AMP 3.
Remove excess liquid from the slides by suctioning with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Place the slides into the slide tray and add one drop per section of RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 AMP 3 solution to entirely cover the tissue.
Load the slide tray into the oven and incubate for 30 min at 40°C.
Wash the slides with 1× Wash Buffer in a slide rack for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Wash again with fresh 1× Wash Buffer for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Pre-warm the RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 HRP solutions for 10 min in a 37°C incubator, then cool to 20°C–24°C prior to use.
Remove excess liquid from the slides by suctioning with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Place the slides into the slide tray and add one drop per section of RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 HRP solution to entirely cover the tissue.
Load the slide tray into the oven and incubate for 15 min at 40°C.
Wash the slides with 1× Wash Buffer in a slide rack for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Wash again with fresh 1× Wash Buffer for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Remove excess liquid from the slides by suctioning with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass dropper pipette.
Place the slides into the slide tray and add approximately 50 μL Opal Dye working solution per section to entirely cover the tissue.
Incubate the slide tray in the oven for 30 min at 40°C.
Wash the slides with 1× Wash Buffer in a slide rack for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Wash the slides again with fresh 1× Wash Buffer for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Pre-warm the RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 HRP blocker solution for 10 min in a 37°C incubator, then cool to 20°C–24°C.
Remove excess liquid from the slides by suctioning with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Place the slides into the slide tray and add one drop per section of the RNAscope Multiplex FL v2 HRP blocker solution to entirely cover the tissue.
Incubate the slide tray in the oven for 15 min at 40°C.
Wash the slides with 1× Wash Buffer in a slide rack for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Wash the slides again with fresh 1× Wash Buffer for 2 min at 20°C–24°C on a rotary shaker (30–40 rpm).
Prepare the IHC dark humidity tray by filling up to 1 mL distilled water into each well between the rails of the tray to keep the tray humidified and prevent slides from drying during staining.
Carefully place the slides on rails of the IHC tray.
Soak several paper towels in distilled water without wringing them out.
Roll the moistened paper towels into cylinders and use them to line the internal walls of an opaque plastic container.
Remove excess liquid from the slides by gently suctioning with a vacuum line fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Lay slides in dark humidity tray and drop approximately 100 μL PBST wash buffer per section onto tissue.
Wash for 10 minutes and suction the liquid with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Wash the slides three times at room temperature (20°C–24°C) in the dark.
Add approximately 50 μL of blocking reagent per section to entirely cover the tissue.
Incubate for 30 - 60 minutes in dark humidity tray at 20°C–24°C.
Dilute primary antibody in Antibody Diluent Buffer.
Remove the blocking reagent by suctioning with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Add approximately 50 μL of diluted primary antibody per section to entirely cover the tissue.
Incubate the slides in dark humidity tray at 4°C for 16–18 hours.
Wash the slides three times in PBST wash buffer for 10 minutes each at room temperature (20°C–24°C) in the dark.
Dilute fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody in Antibody Diluent Buffer.
Add approximately 50 μL of diluted secondary antibody to cover the tissue entirely.
Incubate slides for 1–2 hours in a dark humidified tray at 20°C–24°C.
Wash slides three times in RNase-free PBS for 10 minutes per wash at 20°C–24°C in the dark.
Dilute the Hoechst 500× stock solution with RNase-free PBS (1:500).
Remove excess liquid on the slides by suctioning with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass dropper pipette.
Add approximately 50 μL of diluted Hoechst solution to cover the tissue entirely.
Incubate slides for 10 minutes in the dark in the humidified tray at 20°C–24°C.
Remove excess liquid by suctioning with a vacuum pump fitted with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Add approximately 5 μL of Prolong Gold antifade mounting medium on top of each section.
Carefully place a 24mm × 50mm glass coverslip over the tissue sections.
Avoid producing air bubbles during placement of the coverslip.
Dry slides for at least 24 hours to cure in the dark before proceeding to imaging.
Store mounted slides in −20°C with desiccant for longer storage times.
Select an objective and find the fields to be imaged for RNA puncta counting in DRG samples.
Ensure your slide is clean and dry prior to imaging.
Set image acquisition parameters for each channel.
Choose optimal resolution for the samples.
Select appropriate scan speed for the samples.
Apply frame averaging optimally for quantitative comparison.
Determine excitation line based on fluorescence dyes' spectra.
Define emission collection range according to selected dyes.
Adjust excitation power for maximal resolution and signal-to-noise ratio.
Set master gain for optimal signal quality.
Adjust digital offset for best signal clarity.
Select pinhole size based on imaging parameters.
Ensure imaging bit depth is set to 8 bits when using Airyscan.
Increase scan speed or reduce averaging if noise is observed.
Obtain images of mRNAs in the RNAscope channel with Airyscan module.
Detect discrete or compound (clustered) puncta representing mRNA.
Quantify mRNA puncta within co-stained markers using Z stack images.
Maintain the same imaging parameters across all samples for quantitative comparisons.
Avoid excessive exposure times to limit photobleaching.
